facts.text: The palace was built by architect Juan Bautista Lázaro between 1889 and 1902 as a residence for the Duke of Santo Mauro.
facts.excerpt: The Palace of Santo Mauro was built by architect Juan Bautista Lázaro between 1889 and 1902 as a residence for the Duke of Santo Mauro.

facts.text: The hotel consists of three buildings set in a private garden with fountains and terraces shaded by ancient chestnut trees.
facts.excerpt: consists of three buildings set in a sophisticated private garden, with fountains and terraces shaded by ancient chestnut trees

facts.text: The hotel retains its original interior design, including a Modernist staircase in the entrance hall, a small oval courtyard, an old chapel and the Duke's library.
facts.excerpt: The hotel retains its original interior design, boasting unique details such as the Modernist staircase in the entrance hall, a small oval courtyard, an old chapel, and the Duke's library.

facts.text: The Red Room reflects French Classicism, while oriental pieces in the Chinese Lounge recall objects the Duke collected on his travels.
facts.excerpt: The Red Room reflects pure French Classicism, while the oriental pieces in the Chinese Lounge recall the objects the Duke used to collect on his travels.

facts.text: The ducal family still owns the palace, acting as its stewards.
facts.excerpt: The ducal family still retains ownership of the palace, acting as its stewards.

facts.text: The palace is in the Golden Triangle neighborhood, long the center of aristocratic life in Madrid and home to aristocratic residences, embassies and art galleries.
facts.excerpt: The palace is located in the neighborhood known as the Golden Triangle, which for centuries was the center of aristocratic life in Madrid and has been a popular location for aristocratic residences, embassies, and high-end art galleries.

facts.text: The hotel is in the city center, close to the design area and the city's most renowned museums.
facts.excerpt: The hotel's location, in the city center close to the design area and to the city's most renowned museums

facts.text: The garden was shaped under the guidance of landscape artist Fernando Valero, with fountains and historic trees.
facts.excerpt: Under the guidance of landscape artist Fernando Valero the natural beauty of this space, complemented by its striking fountains and historic trees, invites relaxation, reflection, and reinvigoration.

facts.text: The Duke's Royal Suite was the original Duke's bedroom, with walls covered in green velvet.
facts.excerpt: The Suite Royal The Duke's , was the original Duke's bedroom. The walls are all covered with a marvellous green velvet

facts.text: Designer Lorenzo Castillo designed some of the hotel's most luxurious rooms.
facts.excerpt: Lorenzo Castillo thoughtfully designed some of the most luxury rooms in Santo Mauro hotel.

facts.text: All rooms and suites have marble bathrooms, luxury bedding and high-speed Wi-Fi.
facts.excerpt: All the rooms and suites are designed with high-quality finishes, marble bathrooms, luxury bedding, and high-speed Wi-Fi

facts.text: Evening turndown includes a turned-down bed, slippers set out and local chocolates.
facts.excerpt: a turned-down bed, a bedside mat with your sleepers ready & local chocolates

facts.text: The minibar holds Madrid specialties, including a local wine selected by the sommelier, local pastries and traditional Spanish crisps.
facts.excerpt: The minibar contains some authentic examples of the gastronomy of Madrid: a local wine selected by our sommelier, delicious indigenous pastries and traditional Spanish crisps

facts.text: The Luxury Terrace Suite is a bi-level suite with a garden view and a terrace.

facts.text: The signature Casilda cocktail is served complimentary to in-house guests every day.

facts.text: The hotel offers a walking tour of Madrid's Chamberí district.

facts.text: The hotel keeps a cabinet of curiosities in the tradition of Madrid's aristocratic collectors.
